correctness.rationale: For each third vertex z, weighted distances to the partially exchanged endpoint values are bounded by their original weighted distances plus theta*|w_uz-w_vz|*|f(u)-f(v)|. Convexity of the sum of distances to two endpoints proves the bound, and selecting f(z) equal to the endpoint with the larger incident weight attains equality simultaneously at all z. The edge uv contributes exactly -2*min(theta,1-theta)*w_uv*|gap|. Coarea/layer-cake and constancy preservation reduce the induced variation norm to indicator cuts, whose exact changes give the signed-cut ratio and min-cut test. The simple graph-family classifications follow by counting the unequal endpoint neighborhoods. Exact-rational testing independently checked 4,200 sharp gains, 4,200 cut norm comparisons, 4,200 contractivity decisions, 16,800 direct signal inequalities, 91 star tests, and 480 exact mincut/exhaustive comparisons. The analytic proof, not finite tests, covers all sizes. Two-vertex and theta=0 boundaries are treated separately.

originality.rationale: Published gossip papers supply the pairwise averaging operator and spectral convergence, while graph-total-variation work supplies the variation functional. The materially read 2012 total-variation gossip paper concerns a nonlinear TV-regularized optimization problem, not the variation norm of a conventional pairwise exchange. The result assessed here is the weighted-neighborhood discrepancy equivalence for all graphs, the exact parameter boundary including partial swaps, and the sharp graph-cut/operator-norm formula with minimum-cut decisions. Historical graph-TV contraction and conditional averaging findings concern heat flow or different averaging operators; they do not imply the asserted sharp gossip law without additional calculation. A hidden elementary equivalent remains possible, recorded below.
residual_risks: An equivalent local weighted-neighbor criterion could be implicit in older graph signal processing, Markov operator, or gossip papers despite the search and primary comparisons.
The 2009 graph-regression manuscript was not materially examined beyond its public abstract; it is not counted as whole-document noncoverage.
The elementary structure of the sharp displacement lemma increases the possibility of an overlooked equivalent, although the exact over-relaxation and cut-norm package was not found.

value.rationale: This is an exact stability design criterion for standard local averaging, used in distributed consensus on arbitrary connected weighted communication graphs. It specifies exactly which edges can be updated without increasing graph total variation and how far the exchange may be over-relaxed, while a global induced operator norm and a one-min-cut threshold give quantitative worst-case guarantees when contraction fails. It yields all-schedule pathwise monotonicity criteria and a complete multipartite graph classification; a star demonstrates unbounded one-step variation inflation despite averaging. This is more than an arbitrary numerical constant or routine special-case enumeration. The scientific claim does not include faster consensus rates or other unproved guarantees.
